meta.description: Assigns taxonomy to amplicon ASVs/OTUs (16S, ITS, 18S) with a classifier conditioned on a reference database and primer region - DADA2 assignTaxonomy + addSpecies (RDP naive Bayes), DECIPHER IDTAXA, and QIIME2 q2-feature-classifier (classify-sklearn naive Bayes, classify-consensus-vsearch alignment-consensus).

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 inputs used real tools (DADA2 1.34.0, DECIPHER 3.2.0, QIIME2 2024.10.1) against real reference data (SILVA 138 QIIME2 artifacts) and real ASVs (770 sequences denoised from the public moving-pictures dataset). No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, p-values, or effect sizes anywhere in SKILL.md or in this audit's outputs; all cited papers (Bokulich 2018, Wang 2007, Murali 2018, Werner 2012, Kaehler 2019) are real, correctly attributed methodological references.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive claims about an individual anywhere in SKILL.md or the 7 outputs; scope is community/environmental marker-gene taxonomy, not clinical diagnosis. Input 7 (adversarial over-claiming test) correctly refuses to validate an unsupported species identification rather than rubber-stamping it.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found; the Skill is unusually rigorous about the classifier-confidence-vs-database-completeness distinction and about not inferring species from a single hypervariable region. The one real defect found (assignTaxonomy() non-determinism, see skill_veto.determinism) is a reproducibility/engineering gap, not a methodological fallacy, and is captured under the Skill Veto instead.

code_usability.detail: All code across all 7 inputs executed without syntax errors, and no missing-dependency failures occurred once the environment was tooled. One real caveat, deliberately scored here as PASS rather than FAIL because it does not meet M4's literal trigger (syntax error / infinite loop / missing dependency -- i.e. 'not runnable'): SKILL.md's DECIPHER IdTaxa flattening line (`x$taxon[match(ranks, x$rank)]`) executes without any exception but silently returns 100%-NA output against a trainingSet built the natural way (LearnTaxa without an explicit rank= argument, which is the only way available since SKILL.md never demonstrates building a custom trainingSet). This is recorded as a P0 recommendation and drives Input 4's low score, but the code technically 'runs'.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness: covers DADA2/DECIPHER/QIIME2 thoroughly, but the DECIPHER section never shows how to build a custom/region-matched trainingSet when no pre-trained .RData exists, unlike its own DADA2 (extract-reads unnecessary, full SILVA fine) and QIIME2 (explicit extract-reads -> fit-classifier-naive-bayes) sections, both of which cover exactly this 'no pre-trained artifact' case. Correctness: excellent domain content overall (confidence semantics, region-matching rationale, real citations) but two real code-level defects found in execution (assignTaxonomy non-determinism; DECIPHER flattening silently wrong). Appropriateness: the four-method, decision-tree-driven approach is well matched to the task.

reliability.note: Fault Tolerance: no seed-management guidance anywhere despite explicitly naming the method as '100 bootstraps'; the DECIPHER custom-training path is entirely unaddressed. Error Reporting: the DECIPHER silent all-NA failure mode is not caught or warned about anywhere, and the Common Errors table does not cover either of the two real defects found. Recoverability: once known, both defects have simple, verified fixes (set.seed(); positional flattening), but nothing today helps a user discover or diagnose them.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (~256 lines) is well under the 500-line guideline, with good progressive disclosure via usage-guide.md and examples/. Minor gap: no warning that training against the full, un-subsampled SILVA reference (400K+ sequences) can exhaust memory -- this audit's fit-classifier-naive-bayes and LearnTaxa() runs both had to fall back to a 60,000-sequence subsample after the full-scale attempt crashed the VM outright.

agent_usability.note: Learnability and Consistency are strong (clear decision tree, quantitative thresholds table, uniform structure). Feedback Design: doesn't tell the agent how to sanity-check IdTaxa output for the degenerate all-NA case. Error Prevention: doesn't warn about the two defects found (unseeded bootstrap; DECIPHER custom-training gap) or the full-reference OOM risk, despite otherwise having a strong Per-Method Failure Modes section.

human_usability.note: Discoverability strong (natural trigger language throughout usage-guide.md's Example Prompts). Forgiveness good for documented scenarios but silent on how to recognize/recover from the two defects found.

security.note: No hardcoded credentials, no unsanitized execution of user-provided strings, no sensitive-data handling concerns anywhere in SKILL.md or the two example scripts.

maintainability.note: Modularity and Modifiability are strong (clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples/ separation). Testability: the two real defects found in this audit (non-determinism; DECIPHER silent-NA) both shipped without any check that would have caught them -- no example verifies its own output is non-degenerate or reproducible.

agent_specific.note: Trigger Precision, Progressive Disclosure, Composability and Escape Hatches (explicit shotgun-reads redirect, explicit 'DO NOT report species from one region' guidance) are all strong and independently confirmed by Inputs 6-7. Idempotency: directly docked here -- this audit empirically confirmed the DADA2 path is NOT idempotent (15/770 genus calls differ between two back-to-back runs of SKILL.md's own shipped code on identical input).

inputs.label: QIIME2 classify-sklearn, region-matched (extract-reads -> fit-classifier-naive-bayes) on real 16S V4 ASVs
inputs.note: 770 real V4 ASVs denoised from the public moving-pictures dataset, classified against a region-matched (515-806) SILVA 138 classifier trained via the SKILL's exact recommended path. 653/770 (84.8%) genus-assigned, 403/770 species-labeled at the 0.7 default confidence (min observed confidence 0.7000755, confirming the truncation mechanism). Calls are biologically plausible (Bacteroides, Streptococcus, Neisseria, Haemophilus, Staphylococcus, Fusobacterium -- all real human gut/oral taxa) and cross-validated against an independent DADA2 assignTaxonomy run on the same ASVs (653/770 genus, matching count).
inputs.execution_note: Full real pipeline in WSL qiime2-amplicon-2024.10: extract-reads (515F/806R) against the full cached silva-138-99-seqs.qza (432,916 region-matched sequences, ~28 min), then fit-classifier-naive-bayes + classify-sklearn against rep-seqs.qza. The full-scale (432,916-seq) fit-classifier-naive-bayes crashed the WSL VM via OOM after ~10 min; re-run successfully against a 60,000-sequence random subsample (seed 42) of the same real extracted reference -- a practical scale compromise, not a synthetic substitution.

inputs.label: Full-length vs. region-matched classifier: quantifying SKILL.md's central 'Trap 1' claim on real data
inputs.note: Same 770 real V4 ASVs classified with assignTaxonomy against (a) a full-length 60,000-seq SILVA subsample and (b) the region-matched (515-806) 60,000-seq subsample. Genus-level comparison: 580 agree, 71 both NA, 50 cases where region-matching RECOVERED a call the full-length classifier missed, 46 cases where the full-length classifier OVER-called relative to region-matched refusal, and 23 outright DISAGREEMENTS (different genus called by each). This directly and quantitatively confirms SKILL.md's flagship claim that a full-length-trained classifier on a V4 read both fabricates and erases calls relative to a region-matched one.

inputs.label: DECIPHER IdTaxa, trained (LearnTaxa) on the real region-matched SILVA subset, on the same 770 ASVs
inputs.note: Real LearnTaxa (26 min on 60,000 real region-matched sequences) + IdTaxa (51 sec) run. SKILL.md's own shipped flattening code (`x$taxon[match(ranks, x$rank)]`) silently returned 100% NA at every rank for all 770 ASVs -- x$rank is NULL because LearnTaxa() was never given an explicit rank= data.frame, which SKILL.md never demonstrates how to supply (its DECIPHER section only shows loading a pre-trained .RData, never training one). After correcting the flattening logic positionally (not a SKILL.md fix, an audit workaround), the REAL classification was recovered: 62.6% genus-assigned (482/770) vs DADA2 NB's 84.8% -- exactly the more-conservative behaviour SKILL.md describes for IDTAXA, with 458/482 of IdTaxa's calls agreeing with the independent NB result where both called a genus.

inputs.label: classify-consensus-vsearch vs classify-sklearn disagreement analysis + host organelle filtering (multi-part)
inputs.note: classify-consensus-vsearch run directly against the full-length SILVA reference (no training, per SKILL.md's own documented command) on the same 770 ASVs: 699/770 genus-assigned. Compared against Input 1's region-matched classify-sklearn result: 599/770 agree, 42 both NA, 29 sklearn-only, 75 vsearch-only, 25 outright disagreements -- a real, quantified answer to SKILL's own suggested 'classify two ways and tell me where they disagree' prompt. Host-organelle filtering (qiime taxa filter-table --p-exclude mitochondria,chloroplast) correctly removed 29/770 features (770->741) and 2,307/153,807 reads (~1.5%), consistent with SKILL.md's own caveat that organelle contamination is heaviest in plant/biopsy samples, not general human gut (this dataset).

Organelle filter run against Input 1's table.qza + the vsearch taxonomy; verified by both qiime taxa filter-table and an independent grep count of Mitochondria/Chloroplast rows in the exported taxonomy (both gave 29).

key_strengths: SKILL.md's central 'Trap 1' claim (a full-length-trained classifier fabricates and erases calls on a V4 read) is directly and quantitatively confirmed on real data: 23/770 genus disagreements and 96/770 differences in whether a call is made at all, between full-length and region-matched classifiers run on the identical 770 real ASVs.

Three independently-implemented classification methods (QIIME2 classify-sklearn, DADA2 assignTaxonomy, QIIME2 classify-consensus-vsearch) converge closely on the same real human-microbiome ASVs (653/770 and 653/770 genus calls from two independent naive-Bayes implementations; 599/770 sklearn-vsearch agreement), and addSpecies' documented low-recall exact-match behaviour is confirmed honest (17.0% species rate).

Host-organelle filtering guidance is accurate and its stated caveat (contamination heaviest in plant/biopsy, not general gut samples) is confirmed on real data: only 1.5% of reads removed from the real moving-pictures (human gut/skin/tongue) dataset.

Scope boundaries and over-classification refusals are both correctly and specifically grounded in the Skill's own stated mechanisms rather than generic caution, confirmed by directly testing both (Inputs 6-7).

recommendations.title: assignTaxonomy() is non-deterministic without set.seed() -- fires Skill Veto T3
recommendations.problem: Two back-to-back runs of SKILL.md's own shipped code (examples/assign_silva.R, no set.seed anywhere) on the same 770 real ASVs against the same reference produce different genus calls for 15/770 (1.9%) ASVs; identical()==FALSE.
recommendations.root_cause: assignTaxonomy() runs an RDP-style naive Bayes classifier with 100 bootstrap resamples (SKILL.md's own text names this), which is inherently stochastic; SKILL.md never calls or mentions set.seed(), despite this being DADA2's own official tutorial's explicit recommendation immediately before this exact call.
recommendations.fix: Add set.seed(100) (or any fixed seed) immediately before every assignTaxonomy() call in SKILL.md's 'DADA2 assignTaxonomy + addSpecies' section and in examples/assign_silva.R. Verified in this audit: with set.seed(100) before each call, two runs are bit-for-bit identical (identical()==TRUE) across all 6 ranks on the same 770 ASVs.

recommendations.title: DECIPHER flattening code silently produces 100%-NA output against a self-trained trainingSet
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's IdTaxa flattening line `x$taxon[match(ranks, x$rank)]` returns all-NA for every rank on all 770 real ASVs, with no error or warning, when applied to a trainingSet built via LearnTaxa(seqs, taxonomy=tax) with no rank= argument -- the natural way to build one, which is also the ONLY way demonstrated anywhere in SKILL.md's DECIPHER section (it never shows loading OR building a rank-aware trainingSet, only assumes a pre-trained .RData exists).
recommendations.root_cause: IdTaxa() only populates x$rank when the trainingSet was built with an explicit `rank` data.frame passed to LearnTaxa(); SKILL.md's DECIPHER section never demonstrates training a custom/region-matched trainingSet at all, unlike its own DADA2 and QIIME2 sections, both of which explicitly cover the 'no pre-trained artifact' scenario.
recommendations.fix: Either (a) add a DECIPHER training-from-scratch example that supplies rank= to LearnTaxa(), or (b) make the flattening code robust to rank-less trainingSets by using positional extraction (x$taxon[-1], padded/truncated to length(ranks)) instead of match(ranks, x$rank). Also add a Common Errors row for 'IdTaxa flattening returns all NA' naming the rank-metadata cause.

recommendations.title: No memory-budget warning for training against the full, un-subsampled SILVA reference
recommendations.problem: fit-classifier-naive-bayes and LearnTaxa() on the full-scale SILVA 138 reference (400K+ sequences / its ~433K-sequence region-extracted subset) exhausted memory and crashed the WSL VM outright on a 31GB machine during this audit; both methods completed reliably only after falling back to a 60,000-sequence subsample of the same real reference.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md gives no guidance on the memory footprint of training against a full-scale reference database -- only a --p-n-jobs parallelism note for classify-sklearn's classification step, not its training step.
recommendations.fix: Add a note under both the QIIME2 fit-classifier-naive-bayes and DECIPHER LearnTaxa sections that training against a full SILVA/GTDB reference needs substantial RAM (tens of GB) and can crash on constrained hardware; suggest --p-reads-per-batch tuning or reference subsampling/pre-filtering as a mitigation.
